analysis:
Integration pass across all 13 units. No concrete security regression found. The PR has three parts: docs/changelog text, a coordinator handshake deadline, and a drain-outcome relaxation.

1) Handshake (CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift, CoordinatorClientTypes.swift, CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift). Transport setup is moved unchanged into connectionParameters(for:). TLS is still selected by wss/https scheme, and the plaintext ws:// path was already there. Registration, auth token and attestation are still sent only after .ready, so TB-002 sequencing is preserved. A new 30s deadline bounds TCP, TLS and WS upgrade and cancels and retries via the existing backoff. This improves availability (T-057-adjacent) and changes no trust or authorization state. The handshake source was seen only through prior unit analyses, which report take() under an NSLock so the continuation resumes exactly once. I did not independently see that file. A zero or negative handshakeTimeout only fails the connection, which is an availability matter.

2) Drain (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, head lines ~103-119). .drained is now allowed without a coordinator ack when hasRegisteredConnection() is false. This is gated by nativeOwnersDrained, lifecycleRemaining == 0, the App Attest worker retirement check (workerRetired) and the unchanged refusal of new work (servingDrain.begin). Force semantics are untouched. Accepted work is never truncated; only the ack is waived. A registered session must still ack, otherwise the outcome is timedOut (fail-safe). The race where a registration frame has been sent but sessionRegistered is not yet set (set after sendRegistration in Connection.swift) cannot cause the provider to take work after drained, because admission stays refused locally. Remaining effect: a CLI stop, restart or start may proceed while the coordinator still believes the session is live, which is the same as an ordinary disconnect. No plaintext, key, billing or authorization path is weakened (A-008, A-016, T-053 unaffected).

3) Docs (cli-reference.md, protocol-messages.md, telemetry-schema.md, changelog). These are consistent with the code and do not overclaim. Telemetry still does not claim coordinator_acknowledged=true in the no-session case.

Residual unverified items: the implementations of hasRegisteredConnection() and CoordinatorConnectionHandshake, and the reconnect loop's behaviour after a drained outcome. 45 replayed source units were omitted, so review coverage is incomplete.
